key_insight: Synthetic biomedical data is valuable, but good results in simulation do not always transfer to real-world settings. The paper highlights the persistent simulation-to-reality gap and why closing it is essential for trustworthy biomedical AI.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the challenge of using synthetic datasets to train and evaluate biomedical machine learning models when synthetic performance overestimates real-world performance.
method: Reviews how synthetic data is generated and used in biomedical ML experiments.
Examines the simulation-to-reality gap and why synthetic benchmarks can mislead model assessment.
Frames strategies for turning virtual experiments into more reliable biomedical insight.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work is a reminder that synthetic data should be validated carefully before being treated as a proxy for clinical reality. It helps guide more robust model development, evaluation, and deployment in biomedical applications.
visual_elements: Split pipeline diagram showing synthetic data generation versus real-world deployment
Gap illustration comparing simulated performance and real-world performance
Workflow graphic for training, validation, and external testing with synthetic data
Icon set for data, model, lab/clinic, and uncertainty
paper_title: From virtual experiments to biomedical insight with synthetic data
paper_authors: Margarida Victoriano, Milena Pavlović, Geir Kjetil Sandve, Hélder P. Oliveira, Artur Rocha
